background_notes.fact: For an R-submodule J of C with R=Z_(p) contained in Q, multiplication defines a Q-linear map Q tensor_R J -> C. Every tensor is (1/d) tensor c for a nonzero integer d and c in J; hence this map is injective and has image the Q-linear span of J. A finite R-generating list of J becomes a Q-spanning list. An R-linear decomposition M_R isomorphic to the finite product J^I induces the corresponding Q-linear decomposition after tensoring.

grounds.reason: R is a subring of Q with its specified scalar inclusion into C.
F001 gives the R-submodule J, finite generation and finite coordinate decomposition.
iota and the coordinate identifications respect the specified R-action.

background_notes.justification: The map (q,c) -> qc is R-balanced. Write a tensor as a finite sum q_l tensor c_l and choose a nonzero integer d with d q_l integral. Balancing gives (1/d) tensor sum_l (d q_l)c_l. Its zero product forces the second factor to vanish in C. The image consists exactly of finite rational sums of elements of J. Balancing likewise makes a finite generating list span after tensoring. Tensor the coordinate maps and their inclusions; their composites are identities on pure tensors and thus on the whole tensor product. Finiteness of I permits adding all coordinate inclusions.

background_notes.fact: R=Z_(p) and Q satisfy the strong rank condition. A vector space with a finite spanning list has a finite basis; linear isomorphisms preserve its finite dimension. Over a ring with the strong rank condition a free module with an n-element basis has finrank n.

grounds.reason: Primality ensures the indicated localization is a subring domain of Q.
Z is contained in R, R is contained in Q, and every rational is a quotient of elements of R.
M_R is free over R of rank n.
n is positive and I has n elements.
F002 gives finite dimensionality of T and the Q-linear isomorphism used in the rank comparison.

background_notes.justification: For an injective R-linear map R^a -> R^b, extend its matrix to Q. A nonzero vector in the kernel over Q could be multiplied by a common nonzero integer denominator to give a nonzero kernel vector over R, a contradiction. Thus the extension is injective and a<=b by finite linear algebra. Over Q the same inequality follows by elimination on a matrix. From a finite spanning list delete each vector dependent on the retained vectors; the resulting independent spanning list is a basis. Isomorphisms carry bases to bases, and finite basis cardinality is invariant by the injective dimension inequality. This also identifies natural-valued module rank with n for a finite free basis.

background_notes.fact: For prime integer p and every nonzero rational q, there exist eta in Z and a unit u of R=Z_(p) such that q=p^eta u. For a nonempty finite family of such exponents, its minimum nu is attained, and p^(eta_j-nu) belongs to R for each j.

grounds.reason: p is prime, hence p>=2 and p is nonzero.
Fractions with denominator prime to p are exactly the given elements of R.
The coefficients are nonzero rational numbers in a nonempty finite generating list.

background_notes.justification: Write q=A/B with nonzero integers A,B. Repeatedly remove factors p from A and B; this terminates because their nonzero absolute values decrease at each division by p>=2. Write A=p^s A' and B=p^t B', with A',B' prime to p. Then eta=s-t and u=A'/B'; both u and its inverse lie in R. A finite nonempty list of integers has an attained minimum. Each eta_j-nu is nonnegative, so the corresponding power of p is integral and belongs to R. This verifies the factorization and minimum step already used by S004–S005.
